title: Dungeon furniture sets in blue, green and pink (doors, chairs, tables, bookcases, candelabras, chandeliers, lamps, vases)
player_outcome: The dungeon is furnished with Terraria's dungeon furniture in its brick colour. Chandeliers and lamps light the halls, and you can carry any piece home once Skeletron falls.
design: New data/tileobjects/dungeon.json with 24 objects: {blue,green,pink}_dungeon_ + door, chair, table, bookcase, candelabra, chandelier, lamp and vase.
door: interaction door, size like wooden_door, housing door.
candelabra: light [12,10,6], flame at three points, housing light.
chandelier: anchor Ceiling, size [3,3,3], light [15,13,8], three flames, housing light.
All carry tags [world, dungeon], so their placing items count as obtainable. Use Terraria names ('Blue Dungeon Chair').

Blender: new tools/blender/bgen/dungeon_furniture.py with generators dungeon_chair, dungeon_table, bookcase (with book spines), candelabra, chandelier (iron ring, chains and candles), floor_lamp and vase. Params: palette (blue|green|pink) mapping to prop layers (stone/iron/gold) and tints. The door reuses the stone_door generator with palette params.
Tri budgets: chandelier ≤ 1500, the rest ≤ 800. ≤ 3 material slots so MultiMesh batching stays cheap.
assets.json: 24 object entries. Run build_all.py --only='*_dungeon_*'; object icons for the derived items render automatically.
tests: HousingNavigationTests.DungeonFurnitureCountsForHousing: a room built with blue_dungeon_door, chair, table and candelabra is valid.
Smoke builder.cmds: 'give blue_dungeon_chandelier 1', 'wield blue_dungeon_chandelier', place under a ceiling, 'assert errors == 0'.
verification: tools/blender/preview.py contact sheet of the 8 generators × 3 palettes
risks: The art phase may restyle furniture.py. Keep dungeon generators in their own module.
